subject: Post-demo: model fit recommendations & prompt collection for Acme AI

Subject: Post-demo: model fit recommendations & prompt collection for Acme AI

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move toward a short eval: 

Recap from the call
- Primary goal: generate concise product descriptions from user-submitted feature lists and FAQ-style retrieval answers with low hallucination.
- Data characteristics: high variance in prompt length (15–400 tokens), occasional code/markdown snippets, PII that must be redacted before model exposure.
- Latency target you mentioned: p95 <= 450ms for single-request generation after prefix caching.

Redwood's short recommendations (model fit)
- Baseline: RedLlama-13B (q4f16) for highest quality-per-cost for long-form product text.
- Latency/cost-optimized variant: Mistral-7B-instruct (int8) for shorter completions and chat-like retrieval answers.
- Fallback: RedLlama-7B-compat for constrained hardware regions.

What we need from Acme to run a meaningful eval
1) Prompt set: ~40–100 representative prompts across these buckets: marketing descriptions, retrieval Q&A, code/markdown examples, and edge cases that trigger hallucination. Please include an \"expected behavior\" column where possible (e.g., \"cite source id or return 'no answer'\").
2) Edge-case samples: any prompts that previously caused bad outputs or revealed PII. Mark redaction hints in the spreadsheet.
3) A small sample of real inputs (10–50 items) in JSONL or CSV so we can run tokenization / prefix-cache profiling.

I've attached a prompt-capture-template.csv to this email that covers the columns we find most helpful (id, user_prompt, expected_behavior, success_metric, redaction_hint). If you prefer, drop the file into the secure S3 link you told us about and I can pull it.

Evaluation output and timeline
- We'll run a 5k simulated workload using Redwood Optimize to produce latency/cost profiles and a quality matrix (BLEU/ROUGE where relevant, plus a small human QA pass on a sample).
- Expect preliminary results in ~5 business days after we receive the prompt set and sample data.

Privacy and redaction guidance (short)
- Do not include raw SSNs, full credit card numbers, or passwords in the uploads. If fields contain PII, tag them in the redaction_hint column and we will apply a deterministic redaction step prior to evaluation.
- If you need an NDA, tell us and we'll route the sample intake to our Private deployment team.

Next steps (asks for Jordan)
- Share the prompt spreadsheet (CSV/Google Sheet) and a 10–50 item JSONL sample by EOD Wednesday 2026-09-02 if possible.
- Indicate any absolute do-not-send fields and any compliance constraints we should be aware of.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick <30m follow-up if you'd prefer to walk through the template together.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the sample. Quick answers inline and proposed plan: 

1) Hallucination / chain-of-thought evaluation:
- We will include a targeted hallucination benchmark where we seed the prompt set with known-false facts and check for false assertions. We also run retrieval-augmented prompts with source-citation checks and measure \"source coverage\" as a binary pass/fail per sample.

2) Latency SLOs:
- RedLlama-13B (q4f16) on Dedicated capacity can hit ~p95 300–500ms depending on sequence length and KV-cache effectiveness. For short prompts (<=128 tokens) Mistral-7B-instruct is consistently under 250ms p95 and will be cheaper. Our recommendation is to A/B route by prompt length/intent during rollout.

Proposed timeline and next steps
- Today/Tomorrow: Redwood runs tokenization profiling and a micro-eval on the attached acme-prompt-samples.csv to sanity check outputs.
- Within 5 business days of receiving the full prompt set + sample JSONL: we will deliver a preliminary eval artifact (PDF) with latency/cost tradeoffs, regression concerns flagged, and model recommendations.
- We'll post results to the HubSpot deal and share a results dashboard (link will be posted to the deal).

If that works, can you confirm the S3 upload includes any redaction hints and whether we should expect PII in the sample? Also propose a 30-minute sync on 2026-09-03 at 10:00 AM PT to go over the preliminary findings. I've tentatively added the slot on the calendar and linked it to the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765
